_comment: Cities Without Number, Cyberware Systems chapter (book pp. 62-74) plus the optional 'Cheap Street Cyber' subsystem (p.229, part of the 'Cheap Cyber' optional rules, p.228). Categories mirror the book's own price-table sections (Body/Head/Skin/Limb/Sensory/Medical/Nerve Cyberware); 'Cheap Street Cyber' is kept as its own folder since it's an explicitly optional, separately-priced subsystem the book itself flags as not fitting every campaign. Table columns extracted per item: price, concealment (Medical/Touch/Sight, or 'Obvious' for Medusa Implant), and sysStr (the book's 'SysStr' column, System Strain cost of installation -- fractional for many items). slot is the book's own 'Type' tag column (Body/Head/Skin/Limb/Sensory/Nerve/None), used only to compute the Nerve cyberware +2 Alienation bonus; note some items situated in the Nerve Cyberware chapter section (Skillplug Jack I/II) are tagged Type=Head in the table and do NOT get the +2. permanentStrain = Math.round(sysStr) (schema requires an integer; exact fractional sysStr is preserved in the description text as a documented rounding/schema-gap -- see generator + task report). alienationCost = Math.ceil(sysStr) + (slot === 'Nerve' ? 2 : 0), per the book's explicit Cyber Alienation rule (p.226): 'they gain permanent Alienation equal to its System Strain cost, rounded up to the nearest whole number. If it's Nerve cyberware, this total is increased by +2 per system.' Full Body Conversion is special-cased (alienationOverride: 4) because the book prices/difficulties it 'as if this cyber took 4 System Strain' even though its own SysStr column reads 0 (its real benefit is an effective Con 20 for strain purposes, not a flat strain-max reduction). EMBEDDED TRANSFER ACTIVE EFFECTS: initial empirical testing in the dev world found that `installed` did NOT gate power-item transfer effects for zero-cost-commitment subtypes like cyberware (syncPowerTransferEffects always resolved 'passive' mode to disabled:false regardless of system.installed) -- a real gap in module/helpers/power-effects.mjs, reported rather than worked around. That gap was then fixed (by a concurrent task on this same shared codebase, landing module/config/power-subtypes.mjs#usesInstalledField + the getPowerTransferMode change in power-effects.mjs, plus tests/power-effects.test.mjs) while this import was in progress; the fix was re-verified live in the dev world (drop item uninstalled -> bonus absent; toggle installed -> bonus applies; toggle off -> bonus removed) before any 'effects' were added below. Only items with an unambiguous, already-registered module/config/ae-targets.mjs target get an 'effects' array (Dermal Armor I/II/III, Dermal Armor/Trauma Shielding, Emergency Stabilization Factor, Full Body Conversion, Reaction Booster I, Coordination Augment II, Muscle Fiber Replacement II, Muscle Graft, Skin Plating); everything else -- especially the 'becomes X, or +2 if already higher' pattern (Aesthetic Augmentation Suite, Coordination Augment I, Muscle Fiber Replacement I), which has no floor/upgrade mode for ability .value in the AE registry -- stays narrative-only with an Apply by hand note rather than risk a wrong AE (e.g. an override that would lower an already-higher score). Cyberware Mods (p.74) and standalone Skillplug consumables (p.64, the removable programs -- distinct from the Skillplug Jack/Wiring cyberware itself) are out of scope: mods modify existing gear rather than being cyberware items themselves and there is no fitting-style item type for them in this system, and skillplugs are consumable gear, not implants.

cyberware.name: Aesthetic Augmentation Suite
cyberware.description: Any standard fleshmod can supply beauty, but this suite adds tailored pheromones, vocal harmonizers, social cue triggers, and an absolutely inhuman visual perfection. Apply by hand: the subject's Charisma score becomes 14, or gains a +2 score bonus if already 14 or higher, to a maximum of 18.

cyberware.name: Assisted Glide System
cyberware.description: Retractable nanofiber wings and integral boost jets allow a limited degree of flight. When leaping from a high place, the user gains a flight Move speed of 30m for up to two kilometers before being forced to land. Gaining altitude requires a Dex/Exert skill check against difficulty 10; failure forces a landing, and the wings can't carry the user more than twice as high as the height they jumped from. By deploying the boost jets and wings as an Instant action, the user can ignore up to a hundred meters of falling damage.

cyberware.name: Banshee Module
cyberware.description: Resonant cavities are designed into the user's torso, along with an advanced amplification system. They can reproduce any sound or voice they have heard before, audible clearly up to five hundred meters away at maximum volume. Once per day, as a Main Action, this sound can be used to shatter normal glass in a ten-meter line in front of the user; creatures without ear protection in this area must make a Physical save or take 2d6 non-lethal damage.

cyberware.name: Cybernetic Infrastructure Baseline
cyberware.description: A set of standardized support implants provide a baseline degree of cyber-compatibility to a subject. They can ignore System Strain from cyber implants equal to 12 minus their Constitution score -- so a PC with a Constitution of 9 could ignore three points worth of System Strain from cyber implants. PCs with a Con of 12 or more have no use for this system.

cyberware.name: Deadman Circuit
cyberware.description: A common corporate implant to discourage kidnapping and warelegging. Any attempt to remove any of the user's cyber without the right access codes will fry that hardware unless a difficulty 13 Int/Heal skill check is made.

cyberware.name: Dermal Armor/Trauma Shielding
cyberware.description: A system that can only be installed on a user with at least one level of Dermal Armor, the trauma shielding addition adds +1 to the user's Trauma Target. This benefit stacks with any existing Dermal Armor bonus to the roll.

cyberware.name: Emergency Stabilization Factor
cyberware.description: When brought to zero hit points by an injury that does not instantly kill them, the user automatically stabilizes, gaining one System Strain, and will regain consciousness at the end of the scene with 1 hit point. If they are already at maximum strain, this cyberware does not function.

cyberware.name: Fleshmod
cyberware.description: Careful surgery and support implants allow for a complete physical remolding within generally humanoid lines, including alterations of sex, height, cosmetic limbs such as tails or decorative ears, and overall weight. Reproductive ability is not conferred, but rumors persist of experimental mods that can grant even that.

cyberware.name: Full Body Conversion
cyberware.description:
The user's brain and central nervous system are transplanted into a cutting-edge synthetic shell at a cost and difficulty as if this cyber took 4 System Strain. Once converted, the subject has an effective Constitution of 20 for System Strain purposes, but cannot be healed by conventional first aid or medical drugs, requiring ten minutes of repair work with a toolkit to repair any amount of damage, and $250 worth of parts for each hit point to be restored. A full conversion borg no longer requires food, water, air, or sleep, but each day without the latter adds one System Strain due to the mental stress. The conversion requires twelve hours of maintenance every two weeks, and missing it will result in the user's death in 2d6 days unless the omitted maintenance is performed. Current full-body conversion tech is unstable; after 1d4 years, the subject has a cumulative 5% death chance each year. Borgs do not take Major Injuries and gain a +6 bonus to their Trauma Target that stacks with existing bonuses.

Because the book prices this installation "as if" it took 4 System Strain, this item's Alienation cost is set to 4 even though its own SysStr table entry (and this item's permanent Strain reduction) is 0 -- the real benefit is an effective Con 20 for strain purposes, not a flat strain-max reduction. The +6 Trauma Target is applied automatically; apply the Major Injury immunity by hand.

cyberware.name: Hemosynthetic Filter System
cyberware.description: A wide-spectrum array of blood scrubbers, intake filters, and microbial barriers grants the user effective immunity to most natural diseases and non-synthetic toxins. Weaponized toxins and certain exotic natural afflictions can still affect the user, but they get a +2 bonus on all saving throws against them. The system automatically alerts the user if they have been exposed to a recognized disease or toxin, whether or not it affects them.

cyberware.name: Holdout Cavity
cyberware.description: A biosculpted torso pocket allows for the air-tight, climate-controlled concealment of 2 Encumbrance worth of items inside the user's body and their easy access with a Main Action. Any given object stored can't be larger than a pistol or a tightly-folded suit of clothing, and the pocket's contents don't count against the user's Encumbrance limit. The pocket's signature is disguised against conventional scanning technology, and it cannot be detected without a manual strip search by a trained examiner.

cyberware.name: Medical Support Readout
cyberware.description: A diagnostic system is interfaced with the user's biological processes, allowing a realtime analysis of their current health and any significant injuries. Aside from immediately alerting the user when they are poisoned, diseased, or injured, it grants any healing or medical support skill check made on the user a +2 bonus thanks to the diagnostic information and increases first aid or drug healing by +2 HP per application.

cyberware.name: Recovery Support Unit
cyberware.description: A number of support systems and blood purification filters are installed. The user can absorb up to four points of System Strain incurred from healing or wound stabilization effects; this is a separate pool that recovers one point every night at the same time as the user's natural System Strain recovers.

cyberware.name: Redundant Systems
cyberware.description: Several pieces of prosthetic support cyber are preemptively installed to mitigate future trauma. When the user takes a Major Injury, they may instead choose to have the Redundant Systems critically damaged instead of accepting the major injury roll result. Redundant Systems can be installed more than once, but the System Strain inflicted increases by one point each time (not modeled by this compendium entry -- apply additional installations' Strain cost by hand).

cyberware.name: Retribution Shield
cyberware.description: Numerous small projectile launchers are embedded under synthetic skin. When triggered as an On Turn action, the user gains one System Strain to launch a cloud of shrapnel around them, acting as ground zero of a frag grenade explosion. The user has enough targeting control to avoid hitting allies in range. If grappling or grappled at the time, their opponent automatically takes maximum damage. Reloading the Retribution Shield takes five minutes, and the system will not function if the user is wearing suit-grade armor. Lesser armor can usually be tailored to expose adequate amounts of skin.

cyberware.name: Therapeutic Control Dampers
cyberware.description: A set of customized medical and therapeutic implants are used to control the side-effects of a partially-successful cyberware implant. For each implantation of this system, the user can choose to ignore one implant side-effect they currently suffer. The skill check to implant this system can fail, but it never induces any side effects on its own.

cyberware.name: Titan Gun System
cyberware.description: Usable only by full body conversion cyborgs or subjects with a Strength score of 18, this mount allows the installation of any man-portable Heavy weapon. The user counts as a stable firing rest, and the weapon has two integral magazines of ammo, though it can be loaded by hand as well. The specific weapon mounted can be swapped during maintenance.

cyberware.name: Viper Sting
cyberware.description: A tool of assassins, a Viper Sting is a fang, fingernail needle, palm injector, or more exotic implement for injecting an unsuspecting target with a drug of the user's choice. A Viper Sting can be loaded with up to four doses of pharmaceuticals, dispensed as the user wishes. If loaded with a toxin, it does 1d12 damage with a 1d10/x3 Trauma Die. If a tranquilizer is used, the damage is the same, but unconsciousness will result instead of death. A Viper Sting can only be effectively used as part of an Execution Attack, as an alert opponent can avoid it easily. This cyber inflicts a -2 penalty on any check to detect its presence.

cyberware.name: Courier Memory
cyberware.description: One unit of cranial Memory is installed with a subdermal upload pad. The person uploading the data can set a passphrase; while the implant user can erase the data, they can't download it again without that passphrase, which is usually told only to the data's intended recipient. Courier memory is exceptionally well-hidden and even medical scans take a -2 penalty to find it.

cyberware.name: Cranial Jack
cyberware.description: A discreetly-placed plug socket in the user's head or neck allows interfacing with cyberdecks and gear equipped with a jack line.

cyberware.name: Discretion Insurance Unit
cyberware.description: A small cranial bomb that can be keyed go off when it receives -- or does not receive -- certain codes or transmissions. Its unfortunate tendency to misfire its anti-removal protocols makes it an unpopular choice for use in anyone but the most disposable subjects. Removing this cyber is done at a +2 difficulty, and failure causes the death of the subject and a Physical save to avoid the death of the physician, with 5d6 damage taken on success.

cyberware.name: Eye Mod/Dazzler
cyberware.description: This mod can emit a dazzling strobe of intense light, dazing and disorienting those standing up to five meters in front of the user. The strobe is triggered up to once per round as an On Turn action and adds one System Strain. Victims without eye protection must make a Physical saving throw or take a -4 penalty to their AC and hit rolls for the next 1d6 rounds. A victim can be targeted by this dazzling only once per scene.

cyberware.name: Eye Mod/Flechette Launcher
cyberware.description: A holdout weapon designed for surprise short-ranged attacks, this eye has been loaded with a small explosive flechette. It has the statistics of a light pistol (1d6 damage, 1d8/x2 Trauma Die), has a range of 10 meters, and requires a Main Action to reload its single-round magazine. If used against a target in melee range who does not suspect its existence, a normal hit roll is made; on a miss, it does full normal damage anyway, and on a hit, the damage is doubled. It can be used for Execution Attacks.

cyberware.name: Funes Complex
cyberware.description: A synthetic eidetic memory is granted by this implant, with formalized bodies of knowledge easily cross-referenced and recollected. Once per day, as an Instant action, reroll any failed Int-based skill check. This memory can be difficult to control, however, and unwanted allusions can overwhelm the desired datum. If the user rolls a natural 2 on any Int skill check, it automatically fails and cannot be recovered by any rerolling ability.

cyberware.name: Medusa Implant
cyberware.description:
These prehensile cranial tendrils take multiple forms, from thick armored cables to bundles of brightly-colored articulated polymer fibers not unlike normal hair. The tendrils are shoulder-length under most circumstances, but can extend to manipulate objects up to three meters distant with the agility of a human hand. The bundles are not very strong, however, and cannot lift more than ten kilograms. Like other extra limbs, they do not grant extra actions, but can hold and use items as any other limb could.

Listed in the book as concealment "Obvious," normalized here to Sight.

cyberware.name: Neural Buffer
cyberware.description: A system favored by hackers, a Neural Buffer rearranges the user's brain topography, making it more difficult to harm the user with neural feedback. The user gains an additional 3 hit points per level that can only absorb cyberspace damage from Stun or Kill Verbs. These phantom hit points refresh completely each hour.

cyberware.name: Skull Citadel
cyberware.description: The user's head is augmented with independent blood oxygenation pumps, armor plating, and trauma buffers designed to keep the brain intact even after the rest of the body is critically damaged. Barring dismemberment or the use of high-powered ammunition directly on the target's head, the subject ignores head-affecting Major Injuries and can be stabilized even as long as ten minutes after their technical "death". Each such delayed revivification permanently reduces a randomly-chosen attribute by 2 points, however. This ability damage cannot be undone.

cyberware.name: Dermal Armor I
cyberware.description: Subtle dermal weave reinforcement grants a base ranged and melee Armor Class of 16 and a +1 bonus to the user's Trauma Target.

cyberware.name: Dermal Armor II
cyberware.description: Heavier subcutaneous plating acts as Dermal Armor I with a base ranged and melee AC of 18. In addition, the user can ignore the first instance of Shock in a round (not modeled by an Active Effect -- there is no "ignore first Shock instance" target in the registry, only full Shock immunity; apply by hand). The base-AC bonus does not stack additively with Dermal Armor I/III -- all three target the same innate-AC floor, so having more than one installed simply keeps the highest.

cyberware.name: Dermal Armor III
cyberware.description: Overt ceramic body plating and double-mesh joint reinforcement acts as Dermal Armor II, but with a base ranged and melee AC of 20 and +2 to the user's Trauma Target.

cyberware.name: Poseidon Implants
cyberware.description: These implants allow the user to function normally while submerged for an indefinite period, drawing any necessary oxygen or drinking water from the surrounding salt or freshwater. Normal temperature extremes are managed without difficulty, and pressure can be handled down to depths of one kilometer. Visual augments and pressure gradient sensors allow the equivalent of normal sight up to 30 meters even in lightless water, and miniaturized support jets allow three-dimensional movement at twice the user's normal Move rating.

cyberware.name: Sealed Systems Implant
cyberware.description: When triggered as an Instant action, implanted shields deploy and skin-weaves energize to seal the user off from hostile external environments. For the next six hours, the user can operate as if wearing a vacuum suit, ignoring vacuum, contact poisons, non-immediately-lethal levels of radiation, toxic gases, low or high-pressure atmospheres, and environmental temperature hazards short of open flame. After deployment, the implant needs an equal time of recovery before it can be deployed again.

cyberware.name: Sharkskin Electrodes
cyberware.description: An implanted mesh of electrodes beneath the user's skin allows them to deliver debilitating shocks while grappling a target, even if both are heavily clothed. At the end of each round of grappling, the user inflicts 2d6 non-lethal electrical damage on anyone they grapple or who is grappling them. The shielding built into the cyber automatically negates non-lethal electrical damage for the user and halves lethal shocks.

cyberware.name: Skinmod
cyberware.description: Various neon tattoos, skin texture and color changes, and other superficial physical mods can be performed with no real systemic burden beyond the usual need for regular maintenance.

cyberware.name: Skyborn Shielding
cyberware.description: A set of implants and skin treatments meant for those who spend extended periods in hard vacuum, this implant can be triggered as an Instant action. When deployed, the user gains the benefits of a Sealed Systems Implant and low-G microjets that allow 30m/round flight in microgravity conditions. Skyborn Shielding can operate for up to 72 hours before needing an hour of downtime to regenerate.

cyberware.name: Body Blades I
cyberware.description: Assorted retractable blades and spikes are implanted in the user's limbs. Their unarmed attacks do 1d8 damage, Shock of 2/15, Trauma Die 1d8/x3, and can be rolled with either Stab or Punch as the relevant combat skill. The Punch skill does not add damage to Body Blades attacks. When not in use, the blades are perceptible only to a medical scan.

cyberware.name: Body Blades II
cyberware.description: As Body Blades I, but the user's body armament includes not only conventional blades, but assorted improvements such as monomolecular edges, cutting vibrations, or thermal augmentation. Their unarmed attacks do 2d6 damage with a Shock of 4/15, and a Trauma Die 1d10/x3. Anyone who sees or touches their arms can detect signs of the cyber, however.

cyberware.name: Cyberlimb
cyberware.description: A standard medical-grade cyberlimb, albeit one Encumbrance worth of non-weapon equipment or storage can be implanted in each limb and remain Readied without counting against the character's Encumbrance (add the equipment cost to the limb). The limb provides power to any electronic equipment implanted.

cyberware.name: Iron Hand Aegis
cyberware.description: Absorption plates and kinetic ablation units are implanted in the user's arms and linked with a reactive ballistic calculator. Once per scene, as an Instant action, the user can deflect a successful ranged bullet, arrow, or thrown weapon attack, including burst or suppressive fire. Surprise attacks cannot be deflected this way, nor can melee attacks or explosives.

cyberware.name: Limbgun
cyberware.description: A ranged weapon is implanted into an arm, tail, or other significant limb, along with space for two magazines worth of ammunition. A full reload of this space can be accomplished as a Main Action. Limbguns can be used with Gunlink cyber, count as Readied at all times, and can be used even while both hands are occupied, but can be bound up in melee as normal guns can. Limbguns have an intrinsic +1 hit bonus, in addition to whatever bonus the implanted weapon may have. The maximum size of the gun is Encumbrance 1 for legs or neolimb tails, or Encumbrance 2 for arms. The buyer must supply the gun. Different guns can be swapped in as desired during the system's monthly maintenance, but once implanted, a gun is useless for later conventional use.

cyberware.name: Muscle Fiber Replacement I
cyberware.description: Artificial muscle fibers are implanted as replacements for the user's own flesh. Apply by hand: the subject's Strength score becomes 14, or gains a +2 score bonus if already 14 or higher.

cyberware.name: Muscle Fiber Replacement II
cyberware.description: The subject's Strength score becomes 18. The subject can also smash through standard interior doors or equivalent barriers as a Move action.

cyberware.name: Neolimb
cyberware.description: The user gains an additional limb that normal humans lack. Usual choices involve an additional pair of arms or manipulatory mechano-tentacles, though functional prehensile tails are popular too. One installation of the cyber covers paired limbs or a single tail or body-mounted tendril up to 3 meters long. Neolimbs can support up to one Encumbrance point of non-weaponry built-in tech and add two items to the user's Readied encumbrance allowance. Neolimbs can hold or grip objects, but cannot employ additional shields or grant extra actions.

cyberware.name: Omnihand
cyberware.description: A full array of small mechanical and electronic tools are folded into this cybernetic hand. The user is never without the tools for relevant skill checks, and once per day as an Instant action can gain +1 on any skill check involving the omnihand's tool use. As an improvised weapon, the tools do damage as a knife.

cyberware.name: Shock Fists
cyberware.description: The user's hands are implanted with subdermal electrical webbing. As an Instant action, accept one System Strain; for the rest of the scene, the user's unarmed attacks do an additional 1d8 electrical damage on a successful hit. Unarmed attacks augmented with this mod are non-lethal if desired. This system does not stack with Body Blades.

cyberware.name: Stick Pads
cyberware.description: Macroscale van der Waals generators allow the user's hands and feet to stick to vertical or overhanging surfaces, their full weight supported by one arm. They can climb such surfaces at their full movement rate with one free hand.

cyberware.name: Synthlimb
cyberware.description: A high-grade cyberlimb that's indistinguishable from an organic body part by anything short of a medical examination. It functions as a Cyberlimb for purposes of implanted equipment.

cyberware.name: Active Sense Processor
cyberware.description: Augmented sensory processing. Apply by hand: grants a +1 Wisdom modifier for all skill checks involving sensing or noticing things, to a maximum +2 modifier (when stacked with other such bonuses).

cyberware.name: Cyberears (pair)
cyberware.description: While normal in appearance, touch reveals the synthetic nature of these ears. Some owners prefer to style them in fanciful or unnatural ways. While the base model provides only normal human hearing, all are equipped with ear protection against loud noises. A pair of cyberears or synthears halves the System Strain cost of ear implants.

cyberware.name: Cybereyes (pair)
cyberware.description: While a single cybernetic eye can be implanted, it is recommended that both be replaced at the same time to improve neural adaptation. These cybereyes are clearly artificial, though most are styled in attractive or striking fashions. They all have perfect 20/20 vision and integral flash protectors, but additional functionality must be implanted separately. A user with a pair of cybereyes or syntheyes halves the System Strain cost of cybernetic eye implants.

cyberware.name: Ear Mod/Filter
cyberware.description: The user's sense of hearing is sharpened remarkably, allowing them to follow individual conversations in a noisy crowd, eavesdrop on whispers up to twenty meters distant, and gain a +2 bonus on all hearing-related Notice checks.

cyberware.name: Ear Mod/Positional Detection
cyberware.description: This ear mod constructs a spatial map of significant surrounding sounds, allowing the user to know the exact location of anything making audible noise. The precise location of distant shooters, the location of targets in visual concealment, and the positions of moving creatures in darkness are all clear.

cyberware.name: Ear Mod/Sonar
cyberware.description: The user can navigate even in darkness or while blinded by means of ultrasonic sensors, being able to construct a crude map of people and obstacles in front of them out to 20 meters. This sense is the equivalent of vision, though it can't discern details more subtle than faces.

cyberware.name: Ear Mod/Tracer
cyberware.description: As an On Turn action, the user can nominate a target within 20 meters. Until they get more than 100 meters away from the user or pass behind a solid barrier, the implant's hyper-specific hearing can track their motions perfectly and overhear anything they say or that is said to them. The user can listen to one such target at a time.

cyberware.name: Eye Mod/Impostor
cyberware.description: Aside from allowing free alteration of eye color, this mod allows the user to copy another person's retinal patterns. Provided they are within two meters, they need only meet the user's gaze for a few moments to get a good imprint. The eye can store up to a dozen imprints, but it takes a Main Action to shift from one to another. Note that it is a relatively simple procedure to alter a person's retinal pattern, so an important target alerted to the imposture may end up changing their imprint.

cyberware.name: Eye Mod/Infrared Vision
cyberware.description: The infrared vision this mod allows permits basic navigation in dark areas and makes the presence of heat sources such as humans, engines, and infrared tripwires very obvious. The user gains a +1 bonus on any Notice checks to detect the presence of thermally-unshielded living creatures.

cyberware.name: Eye Mod/Low Light Vision
cyberware.description: This mod grants low-light vision, allowing clear sight to normal distances in any light condition better than pitch blackness.

cyberware.name: Eye Mod/Tactical View
cyberware.description: These eyes can receive text or video transmissions and play them on an inset in the user's normal vision. Outline and pattern discrimination is enhanced; when specifically looking for things or keeping watch, gain a +1 bonus to any relevant Notice check.

cyberware.name: Eye Mod/Zoom
cyberware.description: The user's vision can zoom in on distant targets. The user can see objects within 500 meters as if they were standing next to them. The hit penalty for a ranged weapon's long range is eliminated.

cyberware.name: Gunlink
cyberware.description: Hardwired control points interface with the onboard targeting systems of most modern firearms. When using a modern firearm, the PC ignores range penalties and negates up to 2 points of hit penalties for cover, concealment, or prone targets. Once per scene, as an Instant action, they can reroll a missed attack roll with a gun.

cyberware.name: Headcomm
cyberware.description: An implanted phone/short-range radio that can directly communicate within 100 meters or use the phone grid, if it's available. For cranial security reasons, only text and voice can be transmitted, but conversations can be held without audible vocalization.

cyberware.name: Sensory Recorder
cyberware.description: The user can record up to 180 minutes of sensory input. If they have a jack line into a transmitter or cyberware capable of transmitting data, they can share these recordings in real time or afterwards.

cyberware.name: Synthears (pair)
cyberware.description: This model of artificial ear is designed to be indistinguishable from normal ears, though they have all the properties of a normal pair of cyberears.

cyberware.name: Syntheyes (pair)
cyberware.description: These high-end cybereyes are designed to be indistinguishable from normal eyes under anything short of a medical examination. Any additional mods made to the eyes share this subtlety.

cyberware.name: Prosthetic Cyber I
cyberware.description: One of an array of minimally-adequate and very obvious organ replacements, eye prosthetics, neural patches, and other medical cyber. Prosthetic cyber grants no benefits over ordinary flesh, but can mitigate a Major Injury. Patients who've lost an arm or leg don't need this cyber; they need a serviceable new limb system such as a Cyberlimb or Synthlimb.

cyberware.name: Prosthetic Cyber II
cyberware.description: A more sophisticated and expensive version of basic prosthetic cyber, inobvious to anything but a medical scan and far less burdensome on the user's system.

cyberware.name: Regulated Anagathic Substrate
cyberware.description: This whole-body network of chem regulators can prolong human lifespans by up to 1d4+2 decades. Maintenance on this cyber costs $50,000 a month, however, and interruptions have catastrophic consequences. Rumors persist of even more effective models existing among the megacorp ultra-elite.

cyberware.name: Coordination Augment I
cyberware.description: The user's natural mind-body interface is tightened. Apply by hand: the subject's Dexterity score becomes 14, or gains a +2 score bonus if already 14 or higher.

cyberware.name: Coordination Augment II
cyberware.description: As Coordination Augment I, but the subject's Dexterity score becomes 18, and their base Move rate is increased by 10 meters.

cyberware.name: Enhanced Reflexes I
cyberware.description: Neural acceleration matrices can be deployed to briefly boost the user's reaction speed. Once per scene, as an On Turn action, the user gets a bonus non-cyberspace Main Action.

cyberware.name: Enhanced Reflexes II
cyberware.description: Once per scene, as an On Turn action, the user gains a bonus non-cyberspace Main Action and Move action. By accepting one System Strain, this ability can be used as an Instant action, potentially interrupting incoming attacks if the user moves out of reach.

cyberware.name: Enhanced Reflexes III
cyberware.description: Twice per scene, as an On Turn action up to once per round, the user gains a bonus non-cyberspace Main Action and bonus Move Action. By accepting one System Strain, this ability can be used as an Instant action.

cyberware.name: Reaction Booster I
cyberware.description: These implants grant a +2 bonus to your Initiative, perhaps making you act before the rest of your team. Once per scene, as an Instant action, ignore Snap Attack hit penalties.

cyberware.name: Reaction Booster II
cyberware.description: As Reaction Booster I, but the user automatically wins initiative against targets that don't also automatically win initiative; if both have this ability, initiative is rolled without modifications. The user can act normally during surprise rounds.

cyberware.name: Remote Control Unit
cyberware.description: A neurally-integrated control link allows for near-range control of drones or remote-rigged vehicles.

cyberware.name: Skillplug Jack I
cyberware.description:
A discreet head-mounted plug port allows use of an intellectual skillplug for a skill requiring minimal physical ability, up to level-1 (Know, Fix, or Heal could qualify; Shoot, Exert, or most forms of Perform would not). Once slotted, a skillplug takes fifteen minutes to boot up and integrate properly.

Listed in the book's Nerve Cyberware price table but tagged Type=Head; no Nerve Alienation bonus applies.

cyberware.name: Skillplug Jack II
cyberware.description:
This improved plug jack allows use of either an intellectual skillplug or one requiring physical expertise, up to level-1.

Listed in the book's Nerve Cyberware price table but tagged Type=Head; no Nerve Alienation bonus applies.

cyberware.name: Skillplug Wiring
cyberware.description: A neural wiring connection improves a skillplug jack's limits to allow up to level-3 skill usage. One set of wires can support any number of jacks, but at least one is needed.

cyberware.name: Trajectory Optimization Node
cyberware.description: This cyber can calculate the optimal path for bypassing defenses and striking a target. Once per scene, as an Instant action, turn a missed hit roll into a success. Melee and unarmed attacks can be used as-is, but using this unit with a ranged attack requires an active Gunlink with the weapon.

cyberware.name: Zombie Wires
cyberware.description: Functioning only for a user with at least one Body cybersystem to serve as a motor substrate, "zombie wires" allow a user to keep functioning even at zero hit points. As an Instant action at zero hit points, the user can give their body a one-sentence command involving physical action. Their insensate flesh will blindly carry out that action for up to six rounds until it is complete or they take up to one quarter of their maximum hit points in further damage, which will kill them instantly. Time spent under Zombie Wires counts against a user's stabilization time limit. Triggering this cyber adds 2 System Strain.

cyberware.name: Ballistic Arm
cyberware.description:
A cybernetic arm with a crudely-integrated shotgun or heavy pistol. Works as a limbgun with its +1 bonus to hit, but the weapon can't be replaced and can carry only its own integral magazine of ammunition. Reloading takes one Main Action.

Optional "Cheap Cyber" rule (p.228): low-cost street-grade cyberware, priced and detailed separately from the main cyberware price list.

cyberware.name: Career Mod
cyberware.description:
These system suites of numerous minor tools, mods, and neural adjustments are sold to support a wide range of professions, such as mechanics, drivers, accountants, and courtesans. Once per day, add +1 to a skill check related to the chosen profession as an Instant action.

Optional "Cheap Cyber" rule (p.228).

cyberware.name: Fashion Form
cyberware.description:
Cheap, fast biomodding that sculpts a skin-deep beauty or a niche look suitable for professional performers or companions. Grants a +1 to most social skill checks, but the stigma applies a -1 penalty instead to any skill check reliant on being respected.

Optional "Cheap Cyber" rule (p.228).

cyberware.name: Hydraulic Limbs
cyberware.description:
Requiring skeletal reinforcement and the replacement of both arms, these cyberlimbs grant an effective Strength of 18 for all non-combat purposes and as a Main Action can break, smash, or crush any inanimate object a strong man with a sledgehammer could smash.

Optional "Cheap Cyber" rule (p.228).

cyberware.name: Hype Gland
cyberware.description:
A mentally-triggered chem dispenser that pours a cocktail of combat drugs into the user as an On Turn action. The drugs last for one scene, adding 2 System Strain and increasing the user's effective HP by 10 and granting a +2 bonus to hit rolls and damage, not including Shock. Any excess temporary hit points are lost at the end of the scene. Each year, a hype gland has a 5% chance of causing non-treatable cancer in a user.

Optional "Cheap Cyber" rule (p.228).

cyberware.name: Muscle Graft
cyberware.description:
Crude slabs of muscle and synthetic sinew are stitched onto the user's limbs and torso. Grants a +1 bonus to Strength modifier and a -1 penalty to Charisma modifier (the book caps these at a maximum +2 and minimum -2 respectively if stacked with other sources -- not enforced by this single +1/-1 Active Effect).

Optional "Cheap Cyber" rule (p.228); as a rule, the benefits of this low-grade cyber do not stack with other cyber of a similar kind.

cyberware.name: Nerve Booster
cyberware.description:
Once per day, as a Move action, gain one System Strain and take another Main Action. Incompatible with any other extra-action cyber.

Optional "Cheap Cyber" rule (p.228).

cyberware.name: Razornails
cyberware.description:
Finger-mounted retractable blades that do 1d6+1 damage with 1d6/x3 Trauma Die and 1/15 Shock. They grant +1 to hit with them, using Punch or Stab.

Optional "Cheap Cyber" rule (p.228).

cyberware.name: Skin Plating
cyberware.description:
Grants +2 Ranged/Melee AC, to a maximum of 18 (the cap is not enforced by this Active Effect). It stacks with armor but not with other cyber. It applies a -1 penalty to all Dex skill checks.

Optional "Cheap Cyber" rule (p.228).

cyberware.name: Springheels
cyberware.description:
Compressive pistons are added to a pair of economy-class cyberlegs. As a Move action, the user can gain one System Strain to leap up to 5 meters vertically or 10 meters horizontally, the jump counting as a Fighting Withdrawal for combat purposes. The user ignores falling damage of less than 20 meters. While powerful, the legs are somewhat clumsy, and apply a -1 penalty to all skill checks related to agile leg movement.

Optional "Cheap Cyber" rule (p.228).

cyberware.name: Synthocular
cyberware.description:
A crudely obvious cybernetic eye replacement, usually sold in single units to those who can't afford a pair of tailored cybereyes. Like cybereyes, they come with integral flash protection and halve further eye implant costs. Synthocular users take -2 to all ranged attack rolls.

Optional "Cheap Cyber" rule (p.228).
